correctness.rationale: For arbitrary fields, Goursat kernels A0,B0 and an isomorphism of t-dimensional quotients count exactly the possible S. Splitting their vector spaces shows the bracket-image direct sum has dimension (i−t)(j−t)+(i−t)t+t(j−t)+binom(t,2)=ij−binom(t+1,2), including characteristic 2. For each S, allowable T contain the bracket image and are Gaussian counted; all lifts are precisely Hom(S,Z/T), counted by q^{(i+j−t)(d−e)}. The proof exhausts all subalgebras and proves the dimension formula without hidden generic assumptions. Exhaustive actual RREF and explicit-bracket checks in eight small prime and extension-field cases match every profile; these finite tests only corroborate the general proof.

value.rationale: Subalgebra and index zeta profiles of nilpotent Lie algebras are natural invariants relevant to finite-field and subgroup growth. This gives the entire finite-field subalgebra distribution across a two-parameter family, not an arbitrary small instance. The canonical Goursat coupling index t changes the forced commutator dimension by binom(t+1,2), an effect invisible to prior ideal zeta formulas; the invariant predicts all dimensions and profiles and supplies exact instances such as 15,727 subalgebras at a=b=q=2. No p-adic or unrelated downstream theorem is claimed necessary to confer value.
